focus: Moneybird routing failures and guards for the Product Owner FigJam route
noveltyJustification: The historical hub review provides concrete false positives and false negatives, while the current FigJam specification conflicts with Product Owner’s existing Figma-to-Task signal.
keyQuestions: Which routing mistakes did Moneybird’s reviews uncover, and which controls should Product Owner adopt for FigJam?
answeredQuestions: Which routing mistakes did Moneybird’s reviews uncover, and which controls should Product Owner adopt for FigJam?

label: The first Moneybird hub resolver had confirmed false routes: prefix matching made the CLI signal catch “Jortt clients,” and naming a CLI could send a Jortt-to-Moneybird migration request to the CLI packet alone, bypassing the accountant workflow; later gold rows now pin whole-word matching and the migration chain. Product Owner currently scores the word Figma as a UI-refinement Task signal, while its new specification makes FigJam the requested output; route by explicit output intent such as a dedicated FigJam command or “make a FigJam flow,” keep ordinary Figma feedback in Task Mode, and let mixed source requests begin in Product Owner before any tool handoff. The first filing-gate repair exposed a second defect: testing raw text for a refusal let “Don’t submit anything” suppress a valid purchase-invoice handoff; Product Owner should test negated, quoted, and contextual Figma/CLI mentions so mentions alone never authorize or trigger board writes, which remain gated mutating commands. Moneybird’s initial route suite was green despite four untested mutants, then fresh reviews found more stage-one and negation gaps; the recorded process adds one gold row or failing case per fix and checks that old gold routes do not regress, so Product Owner needs the same build-time route replay and a live plugin/CLI smoke pass as separate checks. The current Moneybird review still reports 46 misses in 741 reviewer prompts and 128 in 5,920 generated combinations, and its audit states that resolver results do not prove a live model follows the route; keep Product Owner’s natural-language router small, use exact commands for high-confidence FigJam intent, and verify representative live routing instead of treating a passing fixture corpus as runtime proof.
